binders: A finite family X1,…,XN of real random variables on one probability space.
hypotheses: For every i, |X_i-E X_i|≤K almost surely.
definitions_and_conventions: The summands are centered by expectation.
σ² is the sum of individual variances.
Probability and almost-sure assertions use the common probability measure.
implicit_context: The X_i are real-valued and the displayed expectations and variances are finite.
The quotients conventionally require K>0 and σ²>0 although neither is separately stated.
If σ²=0, the centered sum is almost surely zero and its positive upper tail is null, but the printed formula needs a limiting or exceptional-case convention.
Only an upper-tail bound is printed.

undebatable_constraints: The bound applies to |X_i-E X_i| almost surely with one common K.
The theorem applies for every t>0.

ambiguities.impact: Ordinary real arithmetic needs K≠0; the standard interpretation is K>0.
At σ²=0 the centered sum is a.s. zero, but the printed expression needs a limiting or exceptional-case convention.

contract_plain_english: For independent real random variables whose centered values are uniformly almost surely bounded by K, let σ² be the sum of their variances and h(u)=(1+u)log(1+u)-u. For every t>0, the centered sum's upper tail is at most exp(-(σ²/K²)h(Kt/σ²)). The printed formula conventionally uses K>0 and σ²>0; zero variance requires an explicit exceptional-case or limiting convention.
